examples: There aren't enough chairs to go around.

senses.head: Circulate — an illness, a story
body: The American counterpart of British go about. (ходить (о болезни, слухах))
examples: Something is going around the office.
A story went around that they'd sold the farm.

senses.head: go around doing — behave in a way that invites comment
body: Followed by an -ing form, and usually disapproving. (разгуливать, вести себя (так-то))
examples: You can't go around telling people that.

senses.head: Take a longer route
body: Of detours around a closure. (объезжать, обходить)
examples: The bridge was out, so we had to go around.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go aROUND
entries.русский: хватить на всех; ходить (о болезни, слухах); объезжать
entries.separable: no — nothing goes between: go around the block, ✗ go the block around.
entries.transitive: either — usually no object; a route or a barrier can follow
entries.verb type: action — dynamic throughout: circulating illnesses and stories, detours, and go around telling people that; the be enough sense is fixed in enough … to go around
entries.passive: no — intransitive, and nothing promotes even when a route follows: ✗ the block was gone around, ✗ the office was gone around by something.
entries.see also: go about, get around, go by

entries.meaning: Attack something or somebody — with fists, or with energy.
examples: The two of them went at each other in the parking lot.
She went at the yard with a machete.
He went at the problem for six hours straight.
They were still going at it when I left.
Give me an hour and I'll go at it again.

senses.head: Attack
body: Of fights: two people going at each other. (наброситься на)
examples: The two of them went at each other in the parking lot.

senses.head: Work at something hard
body: Of chores and problems attacked with force. (рьяно взяться за)
examples: She went at the yard with a machete.
He went at the problem for six hours straight.

senses.head: go at it — argue or work furiously
body: A fixed phrase, always with it. (яростно спорить; вкалывать)
examples: They were still going at it when I left.
Give me an hour and I'll go at it again.

entries.pronunciation note: at is a preposition and leans on the verb — GO at it
entries.separable: no — go at the problem, ✗ go the problem at.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic and forceful in all three senses; the progressive is its home ground: they were still going at it when I left
entries.passive: no — ✗ the problem was gone at for six hours, ✗ the yard was gone at with a machete.
entries.see also: go after, go about, get after

entries.meaning: Leave; or, of a pain or a problem, stop being there.
examples: Go away and let me work.
They went away for the long weekend.
The headache didn't go away until noon.
This lawsuit is not going to go away on its own.
The smell finally went away after a week.

senses.head: Leave; leave town
body: Both the brusque imperative and the vacation sense. (уйти; уехать)
examples: Go away and let me work.
They went away for the long weekend.

senses.head: Stop existing, of a symptom or a problem
body: The subject is the headache, the smell, the lawsuit. (пройти, исчезнуть)
examples: The headache didn't go away until noon.
This lawsuit is not going to go away on its own.
The smell finally went away after a week.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go aWAY
entries.separable: not applicable — no object.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic when a person leaves, and still dynamic, but a gradual change of state, when a headache or a lawsuit goes away
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ the headache was gone away. Gone away is only the perfect: they have gone away for the weekend.
entries.see also: go off, get away, go out

entries.meaning: Return somewhere; or, of a thing or a friendship, date from far back.
examples: I'd rather not go back there.
She went back to school at forty.
The building goes back to 1890.
Their feud goes back thirty years.
He and I go back a long way.

senses.head: Return
body: To a place, a school, a job, a habit. (возвращаться)
examples: I'd rather not go back there.
She went back to school at forty.

senses.head: Date from
body: The subject is a building, a custom, a quarrel; the date follows to. (восходить к, существовать с)
examples: The building goes back to 1890.
Their feud goes back thirty years.

senses.head: go back — of two people, have a long history
body: Always with a stretch of time: we go back years. (давно знать друг друга)
examples: He and I go back a long way.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go BACK
entries.separable: not applicable — no object; a destination arrives through to.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in the returning sense; stative in the building goes back to 1890 and he and I go back a long way, which reject the progressive: ✗ the building is going back to 1890
entries.passive: no — intransitive in every sense, with the destination behind to: ✗ the school was gone back to at forty.
entries.see also: go back on, get back, go over

entries.meaning: Break a promise or an agreement you had made.
examples: He went back on his word within a week.
The company went back on the deal once the funding cleared.
I've never gone back on a promise to my kids.
If they go back on this, we walk.
She would rather lose money than go back on an agreement.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle back carries the stress and on stays weak — go BACK on it
entries.separable: no — go back on your word, ✗ go your word back on.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; it names one act of breaking a promise, so the simple past and the perfect dominate: I've never gone back on a promise
entries.passive: no — ✗ his word was gone back on within a week, ✗ the deal was gone back on. English switches verbs: the deal was broken.
entries.see also: go along with, go through with, give up

entries.meaning: Of time, pass; of a rule, be your guide; of a name, be the one you use.
examples: Three years went by before we spoke again.
Hardly a day goes by that she doesn't call.
Don't go by the photos — see the place in person.
If we go by last year's numbers, we're short.
He goes by Sully.
I'll go by the store on the way home.

senses.head: Pass, of time
body: The subject is the years, the days, the hours. (проходить (о времени))
examples: Three years went by before we spoke again.
Hardly a day goes by that she doesn't call.

senses.head: Be guided by
body: Of rules, appearances, and last year's numbers. (руководствоваться, судить по)
examples: Don't go by the photos — see the place in person.
If we go by last year's numbers, we're short.

senses.head: Be known as
body: Of nicknames and stage names. (зваться, выступать под именем)
examples: He goes by Sully.

senses.head: Stop in briefly
body: American: swing past a place on your way. (заглянуть, заехать)
examples: I'll go by the store on the way home.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go BY
entries.type: phrasal verb (verb + particle); prepositional with an object
entries.separable: no — go by the rules, ✗ go the rules by.
entries.transitive: either — no object in the time sense, an object in the others
entries.verb type: action — dynamic when time passes or you swing past the store; stative-leaning in go by the rules and he goes by Sully, which state a standing fact rather than an act
entries.passive: no — ✗ three years were gone by, ✗ the photos shouldn't be gone by. Gone by survives only as an adjective: in days gone by.
entries.see also: go around, go on, go with

entries.meaning: Fall or decrease; stop working; sink; or, in American slang, happen.
examples: Prices went down after the holidays.
The swelling has gone down a lot.
The whole network went down at nine.
Two planes went down in the same storm.
What's going down tonight?
It will go down as the worst season in team history.
We got there just as the sun was going down.
He went down for eight years.

senses.head: Decrease
body: Of prices, temperatures, swelling, numbers. (снижаться, падать)
examples: Prices went down after the holidays.
The swelling has gone down a lot.

senses.head: Stop working; crash
body: Of networks, servers, planes, and ships. (выйти из строя, рухнуть)
examples: The whole network went down at nine.
Two planes went down in the same storm.

senses.head: Happen
body: Informal and American, usually in the progressive: what's going down? (происходить, твориться)
examples: What's going down tonight?

senses.head: Be recorded, be remembered
body: Always with as or in history. (войти (в историю), запомниться)
examples: It will go down as the worst season in team history.

senses.head: Set, of the sun
body: The subject is the sun or the light. (садиться, заходить)
examples: We got there just as the sun was going down.

senses.head: Be sent to prison
body: Informal, with a sentence length after it. (сесть (в тюрьму))
examples: He went down for eight years.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go DOWN
entries.русский: снижаться, падать; выйти из строя; происходить
entries.separable: not applicable — no object; a place or a route arrives through a preposition.
entries.register: everyday — the happen and prison senses are informal
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in every sense (falling prices, a crashed server, a setting sun, a prison sentence); linking-like in it will go down as the worst season, where as brings a complement, not an object
entries.passive: no — intransitive throughout: ✗ the network was gone down at nine, ✗ eight years were gone down for.
entries.see also: go under, go up, go out

entries.meaning: Perform oral sex on somebody. It is listed here because nothing in go, down, or on warns you: a learner who knows only go down for prices and servers will walk into it.
examples: The script had one character go down on another, and the network cut the line.
Dictionaries label go down on vulgar slang, and the label is doing real work.
A student who learns go down for prices will not guess what go down on means.
In the deposition the witness was asked whether the two had gone down on each other.
Outside a comedy set or a locker room, go down on is not a phrase you use.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle down carries the stress and on stays weak — go DOWN on
entries.separable: no — the person follows the whole phrase: go down on him, go down on somebody. ✗ go him down on, ✗ go down him on.
entries.register: vulgar — sexual slang; it belongs in dialogue and locker rooms, nowhere else
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; vulgar sexual slang, and it belongs to no other class
entries.passive: no — ✗ he was gone down on. The idiom stays active in every register that uses it at all.
entries.see also: go down, get off on, go at

entries.meaning: Choose something; apply to somebody; attack; or sell for a price.
examples: I'll go for the salmon.
In the end they went for the cheaper bid.
Be on time — and that goes for you too.
The dog went for the mail carrier.
The house went for well over asking.
I don't really go for horror movies.
If you want the job, go for it.

senses.head: Choose, opt for
body: The everyday American way to place an order or pick an option. (выбрать, взять)
examples: I'll go for the salmon.
In the end they went for the cheaper bid.

senses.head: Apply equally to
body: Always with a person as the object: that goes for you too. (относиться и к)
examples: Be on time — and that goes for you too.

senses.head: Attack
body: Of dogs and people lunging at somebody. (наброситься на)
examples: The dog went for the mail carrier.

senses.head: Sell for
body: The price follows: what a house or a lot fetched. (уходить за (цену))
examples: The house went for well over asking.

senses.head: Like, be drawn to
body: Usually negative: I don't go for that. (нравиться, быть по вкусу)
examples: I don't really go for horror movies.

senses.head: go for it — take the chance
body: A fixed encouragement with it. (рискни, дерзай)
examples: If you want the job, go for it.

entries.pronunciation note: for is a preposition and reduces to /fər/, with the stress on the verb — GO fer it
entries.русский: выбрать, предпочесть; относиться и к; наброситься; уходить за (цену)
entries.separable: no — go for the cheaper one, ✗ go the cheaper one for.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic when you choose, when a dog lunges, or when a house sells; stative in that goes for you too and I don't go for horror movies: ✗ that is going for you too
entries.passive: no — ✗ the salmon was gone for, ✗ the mail carrier was gone for by the dog. Only the house sold for well over asking rescues sense 4.
entries.see also: go after, go in for, go with

entries.meaning: Be the sort of person who likes or takes part in something.
examples: He doesn't go in for small talk.
They go in for long walks and short holidays.
She never went in for the competitive side of it.
Our family doesn't go in for big weddings.
Where a Londoner says he doesn't go in for sports, a Chicagoan says he isn't into them.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle in carries the stress and for stays weak — go IN fer it
entries.separable: no — go in for long walks, ✗ go long walks in for.
entries.register: British — heard in America but old-fashioned there; the everyday American choice is be into or go for
entries.verb type: stative — it reports a standing disposition, not an act, and resists the progressive: ✗ he isn't going in for small talk
entries.passive: no — stative and prepositional at once: ✗ long walks are gone in for, ✗ small talk isn't gone in for by him.
entries.see also: go for, get into, get in on

entries.meaning: Take up a line of work, treat a subject at length, be spent on something, or enter a state.
examples: Both of her kids went into medicine.
I won't go into the whole history tonight.
He went into it at length in the appendix.
Two years of work went into that report.
She went into labor on the highway.
The car went into a skid on the bridge.

senses.head: Enter a profession or field
body: Of careers chosen: medicine, teaching, politics. (заняться, пойти в)
examples: Both of her kids went into medicine.

senses.head: Treat at length
body: Of explanations you either offer or decline to offer. (вдаваться в, разбирать подробно)
examples: I won't go into the whole history tonight.
He went into it at length in the appendix.

senses.head: Be spent on
body: The subject is the work, the money, or the years that went in. (уйти на (о времени, труде))
examples: Two years of work went into that report.

senses.head: Enter a state
body: Of shock, labor, a skid, a coma — sudden involuntary states. (впасть в, войти в (состояние))
examples: She went into labor on the highway.
The car went into a skid on the bridge.

entries.pronunciation note: into is a preposition; the stress sits on its first syllable — go INtuh it
entries.русский: заняться (профессией); вдаваться в (подробности); уйти на (время, силы)
entries.separable: no — go into the details, ✗ go the details into.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in all four senses: entering a profession, treating a subject at length, time and money spent, and falling into a state (went into a skid)
entries.passive: restricted — only the treat at length sense allows a stiff, formal prepositional passive: the whole history has been gone into elsewhere. The others have none: ✗ medicine was gone into by both her kids, ✗ labor was gone into on the highway.
entries.see also: go in for, get into, go through

entries.meaning: Fire, explode, or sound; leave suddenly; or, of an event, come off a certain way.
examples: The gun went off in his hand.
My alarm goes off at five.
The smoke detector went off while I was searching for the ladder.
He went off to Portland without telling anyone.
The whole event went off without a hitch.
The lights go off at eleven.
In London the milk goes off; in Ohio it goes bad.

senses.head: Explode; discharge
body: Of bombs, fireworks, and guns. (взорваться, выстрелить)
examples: The gun went off in his hand.

senses.head: Sound, of an alarm
body: Of alarms, timers, and smoke detectors. (сработать, зазвонить)
examples: My alarm goes off at five.
The smoke detector went off while I was searching for the ladder.

senses.head: Leave suddenly
body: Usually with to and a destination. (уйти, укатить)
examples: He went off to Portland without telling anyone.

senses.head: Turn out, proceed
body: Always with a manner: without a hitch, badly, smoothly. (пройти (о мероприятии))
examples: The whole event went off without a hitch.

senses.head: Stop working; switch off
body: Of lights and power, the opposite of go on. (гаснуть, отключаться)
examples: The lights go off at eleven.

senses.head: Spoil, of food (British)
body: Americans say go bad. (испортиться (о продуктах))
examples: In London the milk goes off; in Ohio it goes bad.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go OFF
entries.separable: not applicable — no object.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in every sense: guns, alarms, sudden departures, an event that comes off well, and lights switching off
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ the gun was gone off, ✗ the event was gone off without a hitch.
entries.see also: go off on, go out, give off

entries.meaning: Suddenly start yelling at somebody or ranting at them.
examples: He went off on the waiter over a cold plate.
She went off on me for something I hadn't even done.
Don't go off on him until you've heard the whole story.
The coach went off on the referee and got tossed.
My uncle goes off on anyone who mentions the highway project.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle off carries the stress and on stays weak — go OFF on him
entries.separable: no — go off on the waiter, ✗ go the waiter off on.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; a sudden outburst, so the simple past carries most of its uses: he went off on the waiter
entries.passive: no — ✗ the waiter was gone off on, ✗ the referee was gone off on by the coach. American speech says he got yelled at instead.
entries.see also: go off, go at, get after

entries.meaning: Continue; happen; or, as an imperative, keep talking.
examples: The meeting went on for three hours.
Go on — I'm listening.
What's going on out there?
Something strange was going on in that house.
The police had almost nothing to go on.
He goes on about his knee surgery to anyone who'll listen.
The porch light goes on at dusk.

senses.head: Continue
body: Of meetings, arguments, and roads that will not end. (продолжаться)
examples: The meeting went on for three hours.
Go on — I'm listening.

senses.head: Happen
body: Almost always in the progressive: what's going on? (происходить, твориться)
examples: What's going on out there?
Something strange was going on in that house.

senses.head: Have evidence to work with
body: Always with a quantity: something to go on, nothing to go on. (на что опереться, зацепка)
examples: The police had almost nothing to go on.

senses.head: go on about — talk far too long
body: Disapproving, with the topic after about. (разглагольствовать о, талдычить)
examples: He goes on about his knee surgery to anyone who'll listen.

senses.head: Come on, of lights
body: The opposite of go off. (загораться, включаться)
examples: The porch light goes on at dusk.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go ON
entries.separable: not applicable — no object; what you continue with arrives through with.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; the happen sense lives in the progressive (what's going on?), and something to go on is fixed after a quantity word
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ the meeting was gone on for three hours, ✗ his knee surgery is gone on about.
entries.see also: go ahead, go off, get on with

entries.meaning: Leave the house for something social; date somebody; or, of a light or a fire, stop burning.
examples: We hardly ever go out anymore.
They went out for Thai food.
She went out with him for two years.
The candles went out in the draft.
Half the block's power went out.
The invitations went out Monday.
Those collars went out years ago.

senses.head: Leave home for something social
body: Dinner, a movie, a bar. (выходить, идти куда-то (развлечься))
examples: We hardly ever go out anymore.
They went out for Thai food.

senses.head: Date somebody
body: With with; the standard American phrase for seeing someone. (встречаться с)
examples: She went out with him for two years.

senses.head: Stop burning or shining
body: Of candles, fires, and the power. (гаснуть, отключаться)
examples: The candles went out in the draft.
Half the block's power went out.

senses.head: Be sent or broadcast
body: Of invitations, notices, and signals. (быть разосланным, выйти в эфир)
examples: The invitations went out Monday.

senses.head: Go out of style
body: Of fashions that have had their day. (выйти из моды)
examples: Those collars went out years ago.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go OUT
entries.separable: not applicable — no object; a companion arrives through with: go out with Dana, ✗ go Dana out.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in all five senses; go out with is the dating frame and leaves the verb intransitive
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ the candles were gone out in the draft, ✗ he was gone out with for two years. Sense 4 already reads as a passive without it: the invitations went out Monday.
entries.see also: go away, get out, go off

entries.meaning: Review something carefully; be received a certain way; or cross to the other side.
examples: Let's go over the numbers one more time.
She went over my essay line by line.
The joke did not go over well.
His apology went over better than expected.
We went over budget by nine thousand dollars.
We went over the pass at dawn.

senses.head: Review, examine
body: Of numbers, drafts, and plans checked line by line. (разобрать, просмотреть)
examples: Let's go over the numbers one more time.
She went over my essay line by line.

senses.head: Be received in a certain way
body: Always with well, badly, or like a lead balloon. (быть принятым (хорошо/плохо))
examples: The joke did not go over well.
His apology went over better than expected.

senses.head: Exceed
body: Of budgets, time limits, and word counts. (превысить, выйти за)
examples: We went over budget by nine thousand dollars.

senses.head: Cross
body: The literal sense: travel across something. (перебраться через)
examples: We went over the pass at dawn.

entries.pronunciation note: the stress falls on over — go Over it
entries.separable: no — go over the numbers, never ✗ go the numbers over.
entries.transitive: either — an object when you review something, none when a joke goes over well
entries.verb type: action — dynamic when you review, exceed a budget, or cross a pass; the be received sense (the joke didn't go over well) is dynamic too, but demands a manner word
entries.passive: restricted — the review sense takes a prepositional passive: the numbers had been gone over twice before the meeting. The others refuse it: ✗ the budget was gone over by nine thousand dollars, ✗ the joke was gone over well.
entries.see also: go through, get over, go under

entries.meaning: Live through something hard; search something thoroughly; or, of a deal, be completed.
examples: Nobody should have to go through that twice.
She went through chemo last spring.
He went through every drawer in the house.
The sale went through on Friday.
If the loan doesn't go through, we're out.
The twins go through a gallon of milk a day.
Let's go through it once more before the demo.

senses.head: Experience, endure
body: Of illness, grief, divorce — the hard stretches. (пережить, пройти через)
examples: Nobody should have to go through that twice.
She went through chemo last spring.

senses.head: Search thoroughly
body: Of drawers, files, and pockets turned out one by one. (перерыть, обыскать)
examples: He went through every drawer in the house.

senses.head: Be approved, be completed
body: Of sales, loans, and permits; no object. (состояться, пройти)
examples: The sale went through on Friday.
If the loan doesn't go through, we're out.

senses.head: Use up
body: Of milk, batteries, money — supplies that vanish fast. (израсходовать, уходить (о запасах))
examples: The twins go through a gallon of milk a day.

senses.head: Review step by step
body: Of rehearsals and walkthroughs. (пройтись по, повторить)
examples: Let's go through it once more before the demo.

entries.pronunciation note: the stress falls on through — go THROUGH it
entries.separable: no — go through the drawers, ✗ go the drawers through. (The separable get something through belongs to get, not go.)
entries.transitive: either — an object in most senses, none when a deal goes through
entries.verb type: action — dynamic throughout: enduring a hard stretch, searching, using up supplies, rehearsing, and a sale that clears
entries.passive: restricted — natural in the search sense: every drawer in the house had been gone through. Not in the others: ✗ chemo was gone through last spring, ✗ a gallon of milk is gone through daily; the be approved sense is intransitive already.
entries.see also: go through with, go over, get through

entries.meaning: Do the difficult thing you said you would do, in spite of second thoughts.
examples: She couldn't go through with the wedding.
He went through with the surgery after all.
They threatened to sue and then actually went through with it.
I don't think he'll go through with it.
Once the deposit was paid we had to go through with the move.
entries.pronunciation note: through carries the stress and with stays weak — go THROUGH with it
entries.separable: no — go through with the plan, ✗ go the plan through with.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; it names carrying out a decision you had second thoughts about, and the object is nearly always it or an event noun
entries.passive: no — ✗ the wedding was gone through with, ✗ the surgery was gone through with after all. Use the surgery went ahead instead.
entries.see also: go through, go ahead, go back on

entries.meaning: Fail as a business, sink, or lose consciousness on an operating table.
examples: Three restaurants on that block went under in a year.
The company went under before the loan cleared.
The boat went under in less than a minute.
Count backward from ten — you'll go under fast.
He went under at ten and woke up at two.

senses.head: Fail, go bankrupt
body: Of businesses that run out of money. (обанкротиться, прогореть)
examples: Three restaurants on that block went under in a year.
The company went under before the loan cleared.

senses.head: Sink
body: Of boats and swimmers. (пойти ко дну, утонуть)
examples: The boat went under in less than a minute.

senses.head: Lose consciousness under anesthesia
body: Informal, from the patient's side of it. (отключиться (под наркозом))
examples: Count backward from ten — you'll go under fast.
He went under at ten and woke up at two.

entries.pronunciation note: the stress falls on under — go UNder
entries.separable: not applicable — no object.
entries.register: everyday — the anesthesia sense is informal
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; each sense names a change of state — a business fails, a boat sinks, a patient loses consciousness
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ the company was gone under before the loan cleared.
entries.see also: go down, go up, go through

entries.meaning: Rise or increase; be built; or, with in flames, burn.
examples: Rent went up again in June.
Her temperature has gone up since this morning.
Two new towers went up on the waterfront.
The barn went up in about four minutes.
Ten years of savings went up in smoke.
He went up to her and introduced himself.

senses.head: Increase
body: Of rent, prices, temperatures, and fevers. (расти, повышаться)
examples: Rent went up again in June.
Her temperature has gone up since this morning.

senses.head: Be built
body: Of buildings rising on a lot. (строиться, возводиться)
examples: Two new towers went up on the waterfront.

senses.head: Burn or explode
body: Always with in flames or in smoke. (сгореть, взлететь на воздух)
examples: The barn went up in about four minutes.
Ten years of savings went up in smoke.

senses.head: go up to — approach
body: With a person as the object of to. (подойти к)
examples: He went up to her and introduced himself.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — go UP
entries.separable: not applicable — no object; a target arrives through to.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in all four senses; go up in flames and go up in smoke are fixed with that complement
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ the rent was gone up in June, ✗ she was gone up to and introduced to.
entries.see also: go down, go under, grow up

entries.meaning: Match something; settle on an option; or come as part of a package.
examples: That tie doesn't go with the shirt.
A dry white goes with the fish.
Let's go with the blue one.
We went with the local contractor.
A parking space goes with the apartment.
I'll go with you.

senses.head: Match, suit
body: Of clothes, colors, and food and wine. (подходить к, сочетаться с)
examples: That tie doesn't go with the shirt.
A dry white goes with the fish.

senses.head: Choose, settle on
body: The decision sense, very common in American offices. (остановиться на, выбрать)
examples: Let's go with the blue one.
We went with the local contractor.

senses.head: Come as part of
body: The subject is what is included. (прилагаться к, идти в комплекте)
examples: A parking space goes with the apartment.

senses.head: Accompany
body: The literal sense, with a person. (пойти с)
examples: I'll go with you.

entries.pronunciation note: with is a preposition and leans on the verb — GO with it
entries.русский: подходить к, сочетаться с; остановиться на (варианте)
entries.separable: no — go with the blue one, ✗ go the blue one with.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic when you settle on an option or accompany someone (let's go with the blue one); stative in the matching and included-with senses, which reject the progressive: ✗ that tie isn't going with the shirt, ✗ a parking space is going with the apartment
entries.passive: no — ✗ the local contractor was gone with, ✗ the fish is gone with by a dry white. Say we chose the local contractor.
entries.see also: go for, go along with, go without

entries.meaning: Manage without something you need or want.
examples: They went without heat for a week in January.
If there isn't enough, I'll go without.
She went without lunch to make the deadline.
Nobody in that house ever went without.
You can go without sleep for one night, but not for three.
entries.pronunciation note: the stress falls on the second syllable of without — go withOUT
entries.separable: no — go without heat, ✗ go heat without.
entries.transitive: either — the object can be left off entirely: I'll go without
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; it covers a stretch of doing without, so the past and perfect are its usual tenses: they went without heat for a week
entries.passive: no — ✗ heat was gone without for a week, ✗ lunch was gone without. The object is optional anyway: I'll go without.
entries.see also: go with, get by, give up

entries.meaning: Keep working at something slow and tiring; or wear a surface off a little at a time.
examples: He grinds away at the same spreadsheet every quarter.
She ground away at her dissertation for six years.
The two of them have been grinding away since seven this morning.
Somewhere in the basement a fan was grinding away.
You grind away long enough and eventually the thing is finished.
Grind the old weld away before you start anything else.
The shop ground away two decades of rust in an afternoon.
The sea has been grinding it away since the lighthouse went up.

senses.head: Keep working, with no end in sight
body: No object; the job you are stuck on arrives through at. (корпеть, вкалывать)
examples: He grinds away at the same spreadsheet every quarter.
She ground away at her dissertation for six years.
The two of them have been grinding away since seven this morning.
Somewhere in the basement a fan was grinding away.
You grind away long enough and eventually the thing is finished.

senses.head: Wear away by grinding
body: Of rust, paint, welds, and cliffs. The object sits on either side of away, and a pronoun sits in front of it. (стачивать, счищать)
examples: Grind the old weld away before you start anything else.
The shop ground away two decades of rust in an afternoon.
The sea has been grinding it away since the lighthouse went up.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — grind aWAY
entries.separable: yes in the wear away sense — grind the rust away or grind away the rust, and a pronoun must split: grind it away, never ✗ grind away it. In the keep working sense there is no object to place at all; the job arrives through at: grind away at the report, ✗ grind the report away.
entries.transitive: either — no object when you keep working, an object when you wear something away
entries.verb type: action — dynamic and durative in both senses; the progressive is its natural home: they've been grinding away since seven this morning
entries.passive: restricted — the transitive wear away sense passivizes cleanly: two decades of rust were ground away in an afternoon. The keep working sense is intransitive and has none: ✗ the dissertation was ground away at for six years.
entries.see also: grind on, grind out, get down to

entries.meaning: Wear somebody out until they stop resisting; or wear a surface away by friction.
examples: Twelve-hour shifts grind people down.
The lawsuit ground him down over four years.
Their whole strategy is to grind you down with paperwork.
Years of chewing ice had ground her molars down.
The glacier ground down the whole ridge.

senses.head: Wear somebody out until they give in
body: Of shifts, lawsuits, and tactics designed to exhaust you. (изматывать, доводить до изнеможения)
examples: Twelve-hour shifts grind people down.
The lawsuit ground him down over four years.
Their whole strategy is to grind you down with paperwork.

senses.head: Wear away by friction
body: The literal sense, of teeth, stone, and glaciers. (стачивать, стирать)
examples: Years of chewing ice had ground her molars down.
The glacier ground down the whole ridge.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — grind them DOWN
entries.separable: yes — grind the opposition down or grind down the opposition, and a pronoun must split: grind them down, never ✗ grind down them.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic, and gradual in both senses, so the progressive suits it: the lawsuit was grinding him down
entries.passive: yes — he was ground down by four years of litigation, her molars had been ground down by years of chewing ice.
entries.see also: grind on, grind out, get through

entries.meaning: Continue slowly and tediously, well past the point where anyone wanted it to stop.
examples: The hearing ground on into a third week.
The war ground on for another two years.
His speech ground on while the room quietly emptied.
Negotiations have been grinding on since March.
The season grinds on whether you're healthy or not.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — grind ON
entries.separable: not applicable — no object.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic and durative; it names a tedious continuation, at home in both the simple past and the progressive: negotiations have been grinding on since March
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ the hearing was ground on into a third week.
entries.see also: grind away, grind down, go on

entries.meaning: Produce something steadily and joylessly; or win something ugly through sheer effort.
examples: He grinds out two columns a week.
The studio ground them out four a year.
They ground out a 3-1 win in the rain.
She ground the last mile out on a bad ankle.
He ground his cigarette out on the step.

senses.head: Produce steadily, without inspiration
body: Of columns, sequels, and reports turned out on schedule. (штамповать, выдавать)
examples: He grinds out two columns a week.
The studio ground them out four a year.

senses.head: Win or achieve through effort alone
body: Sports usage: no style, just result. (вырвать (победу), выгрызть)
examples: They ground out a 3-1 win in the rain.
She ground the last mile out on a bad ankle.

senses.head: Extinguish by twisting
body: Of cigarettes pressed out underfoot. (затушить, потушить (окурок))
examples: He ground his cigarette out on the step.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — grind them OUT
entries.separable: yes — grind out another chapter or grind another chapter out, and a pronoun must split: grind them out, never ✗ grind out them.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in all three senses: producing on schedule, winning ugly, and stubbing out a cigarette
entries.passive: yes — two columns a week are ground out on deadline, a 3-1 win was ground out in the rain, the cigarette was ground out on the step.
entries.see also: grind away, grind down, give out

entries.meaning: Slowly lose closeness with somebody you used to be close to, without any quarrel.
examples: They didn't fight about anything; they just grew apart.
We grew apart after high school.
The brothers had grown apart by the time their mother died.
Couples grow apart when nobody notices it happening.
It's easy to grow apart when you live two time zones away.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — grow aPART
entries.separable: not applicable — no object; the phrase describes two people together.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic, but a slow process rather than an event, so the progressive fits: they were growing apart for years before anyone said so
entries.passive: no — intransitive, and it takes a joint or plural subject: ✗ the brothers were grown apart, ✗ he was grown apart from.
entries.see also: grow up, grow out of, go back

entries.meaning: Return by growing after being cut, lost, or damaged — or regrow the part you lost.
examples: His hair grew back thicker after the treatment.
Cut the basil hard and it grows back within a week.
The lawn never grew back where the pool had been.
Her nails had grown back by the spring.
A lizard grows its tail back; a person cannot grow back a finger.
He shaved in June and grew the beard back by August.
It took two years to grow it back after the chemo.

senses.head: Return by growing
body: No object; the hair, the grass, or the tail is the subject. (отрасти заново, вырасти снова)
examples: His hair grew back thicker after the treatment.
Cut the basil hard and it grows back within a week.
The lawn never grew back where the pool had been.
Her nails had grown back by the spring.

senses.head: Regrow something you lost
body: Now there is an object, and it may sit on either side of back; a pronoun sits in front of it. (отрастить обратно, восстановить)
examples: A lizard grows its tail back; a person cannot grow back a finger.
He shaved in June and grew the beard back by August.
It took two years to grow it back after the chemo.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — grow it BACK
entries.русский: отрасти заново, вырасти снова; отрастить обратно
entries.separable: yes when there is an object — grow its tail back or grow back its tail, and a pronoun must split: grow it back, never ✗ grow back it. Most of the time, though, what returns is simply the subject and there is nothing to place: his hair grew back.
entries.transitive: either — no object when the thing returns on its own, an object when somebody regrows it
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; sense 1 is a process the subject undergoes (his hair grew back), sense 2 an act with an object (he grew the beard back by August)
entries.passive: restricted — acceptable only in generic statements about what can regrow: a tail can be grown back; a finger cannot. Awkward for a real event: ✗ the beard was grown back by August, and sense 1 is intransitive with no passive at all.
entries.see also: grow into, grow up, get back

entries.meaning: Become big enough for something, or develop until you fit a role.
examples: Buy the coat a size up — he'll grow into it.
She grew into the job in about a year.
He has grown into a careful, patient teacher.
The reading group grew into a small press.
What started as a hobby grew into a business.

senses.head: Become big enough for
body: Of children's clothes bought a size too large. (дорасти до (одежды))
examples: Buy the coat a size up — he'll grow into it.

senses.head: Develop into a role
body: Of jobs and responsibilities that fit badly at first. (войти в роль, дорасти до)
examples: She grew into the job in about a year.
He has grown into a careful, patient teacher.

senses.head: Develop into something larger
body: Of small projects that turn into big ones. (перерасти в, превратиться в)
examples: The reading group grew into a small press.
What started as a hobby grew into a business.

entries.pronunciation note: into is a preposition; the stress sits on its first syllable — grow INtuh it
entries.русский: дорасти до (одежды); войти в (роль); перерасти в
entries.separable: no — grow into the coat, ✗ grow the coat into.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; every sense is a gradual development, which is why the perfect is so common: he has grown into a careful, patient teacher
entries.passive: no — ✗ the coat will be grown into, ✗ the job was grown into in about a year. Say she settled into the job.
entries.see also: grow out of, grow up, get into

entries.meaning: Come to be liked by somebody gradually, after a poor or flat first impression.
examples: I hated the album at first, but it grew on me.
Give the town a year — it grows on you.
The name has grown on everybody in the office.
That painting never grew on me.
His sense of humor grows on people slowly.
entries.pronunciation note: the stress falls on on — it grew ON me
entries.separable: no — the person always follows the whole phrase: the song grew on me, ✗ the song grew me on.
entries.transitive: yes, always takes an object — the person who comes to like it
entries.verb type: action — dynamic but gradual, with the thing as subject and the person as object; the progressive works: the town is growing on me
entries.passive: no — the experiencer has to stay the object: ✗ I was grown on by the album, ✗ everybody in the office has been grown on. English says I came to like it.
entries.see also: grow into, get into, go for

entries.meaning: Get too big for something, leave a habit behind, or originate in something smaller.
examples: She grew out of those boots in one winter.
Most kids grow out of it by six.
He never grew out of correcting people.
The company grew out of a college project.
The law grew out of a single case in Ohio.

senses.head: Get too big for
body: Of clothes and shoes outgrown in a season. (вырасти из (одежды))
examples: She grew out of those boots in one winter.

senses.head: Leave a habit or a phase behind
body: Of tantrums, allergies, and phases parents wait out. (перерасти, избавиться с возрастом)
examples: Most kids grow out of it by six.
He never grew out of correcting people.

senses.head: Originate in
body: Of companies, laws, and books that began as something else. (вырасти из, возникнуть из)
examples: The company grew out of a college project.
The law grew out of a single case in Ohio.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle out carries the stress and of reduces to /əv/ — grow OUT uv it
entries.separable: no — grow out of those boots, ✗ grow those boots out of.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in senses 1 and 2 (outgrowing boots, outgrowing tantrums); stative in sense 3, a standing fact of origin: ✗ the company is growing out of a college project
entries.passive: no — ✗ those boots were grown out of in one winter, ✗ a college project was grown out of by the company.
entries.see also: grow into, grow up, get over

entries.meaning: Become an adult; spend your childhood somewhere; or, as a rebuke, start acting like one.
examples: I grew up just outside Cleveland.
Kids grow up faster than their parents expect.
Grow up and apologize to her.
A whole town grew up around the mill.
A market for used parts has grown up online.

senses.head: Become an adult; spend childhood somewhere
body: The core sense, with a place or a period after it. (расти, взрослеть)
examples: I grew up just outside Cleveland.
Kids grow up faster than their parents expect.

senses.head: Grow up! — act your age
body: An imperative, sharp and dismissive. (повзрослей!, хватит ребячиться)
examples: Grow up and apologize to her.

senses.head: Develop, of a place or a practice
body: Of towns and markets that form around something. (вырасти, сложиться)
examples: A whole town grew up around the mill.
A market for used parts has grown up online.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle takes the stress — grow UP
entries.русский: расти, взрослеть; повзрослеть (веди себя как взрослый)
entries.separable: not applicable — no object. Raising a child is bring up or raise, not ✗ grow a child up.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in all three senses; the imperative Grow up! is a rebuke, not a separate class, and grown up in she's all grown up is an adjective, not a passive participle
entries.passive: no — intransitive: ✗ Cleveland was grown up outside of, ✗ the mill was grown up around. Raising a child uses another verb: she was brought up in Ohio.
entries.see also: grow apart, grow into, go up
